ai.description: The Hill Keelback reaches 60 cm. It is olive-brown with a distinct yellow nuchal collar and a dark postocular streak. The body features strongly keeled scales and a pale, checkered belly.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Hill Keelback is best identified by the prominent, bright yellow or white V-shaped mark on the nape of its neck, which distinguishes it from other similar keelbacks.
ai.habitat: The Hill Keelback inhabits evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found near streams at mid-to-high elevations between 600 and 1,800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Hill Keelback is primarily diurnal and specializes in foraging for frogs and tadpoles along the rocky, fast-flowing streams of the Western Ghats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Amphiesma monticola* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–6 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing shortly thereafter.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Hill Keelback (*Amphiesma monticola*) is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in evergreen forests at elevations between 700 and 1,500 meters.
